summary: Tested which premise separates a necessary physical ground from a classical ground. Findings: one necessity signature (necessary, underived, capacity, esse-cause of a contingent other) is shared by five route tables, so it yields no maximum, simplicity, immateriality, intellect or will. The strongest composite rival denies exactly the uniting-cause premise; a part-free impersonal rival denies exactly q.14 a.1; will is separated by q.19 a.1. Formal containment separates the grounds only given a classification of respects: two classifications favour opposite grounds, and the one independent of the candidate turns on which simple beings the table has. A physicalist bearer bundle excludes the classical ground, conditional on its three Papineau premises and two bearer premises. On four shared explananda neither ground gains in the encoded terms; contingency-of-laws selection takes no attribute. Rejected: importing Hume's Dialogues IX as an attribution, because no passage is pinned. Rejected: defining physical as composite outright, because a part-free ground may be physical in Papineau's sense. Rejected: flags for personhood as a discriminator; the flag appears only in the explicit bridge MarksRequirePerson. Details in docs/notes/physical-ground-468.md. Follow-up 2026-11-03: materialized SPINOZA-ETHICS-ELWES-FULL and read Ethics I 13-20, 29-35 and II 1-3 with proofs and notes as the strongest historical source for a necessary impersonal ground. Finding: Spinoza keeps a maximum (I def. 6), indivisibility (I 13), essence-existence identity (I 20) and uniqueness of substance (I 14), so he takes none of the ladder's maximum, composite or simplicity exits; he denies the Signature's contingent effect (I 29, I 33) and free will (I 32), placing his rival on #555's necessitarian branch (SIMPLICITY-BRANCH-COSTS). His extended but indivisible substance (I 13 cor., I 15 note) supports not defining physical as composite. Whether HasIntellect holds of his God splits on two defensible readings (II 1, II 3 versus I 31, I 17 note); neither is formalized. I 33 note II supplies the collapse argument #555 tests (identity of intellect, will and essence plus eternal decrees gives a different essence for a different order); the classical reply read in q.19 a.3 ad 5-6 is #555's optional-act exit. Rejected: attributing the ladder's esse-support, ConcreteAt or accessible-world necessity to Spinoza; equating his sense of free cause (I def. 7) with HasWill; reading his denial of free will (I 32) as a denial of HasWill on reading A, since DEF-HAS-WILL requires no contingent choice, so the will rung stays unresolved for that reading.
blocker: Independent defense of the uniting-cause premise for a necessary composite, of a maximum for a necessary ground, of q.14 a.1 from a negative antecedent, and of any classification of respects remains open. No theory of laws, of a necessary initial state's identity across Oppy's restricted worlds, or of self-explanation is supplied. No root premise is discharged. Against the Spinozist rival specifically, the open step is that some effect of the ground is contingent or that a nonnecessitating reason is adequate; maximum, simplicity and uniqueness steps do not separate it. No pinned witness for a contemporary composite-whole physical monism.
